reasoning:
All organisms have pieces of hereditary material called genes, which are passed from parents to offspring. Genes contain instructions for building the parts of an organism. An organism's genes affect its observable traits, including its appearance, its behavior, and which diseases it may have. Genes may have different alleles, or forms, that can cause different versions of a trait.
For example, flower color is a trait in pea plants. The gene for this trait has two possible alleles. Each allele is represented by an uppercase or lowercase letter. The allele F is for purple flowers, and the allele f is for white flowers. Each pea plant has two alleles for the flower color gene—one allele inherited from each parent.
An organism's genotype for a gene is its combination of alleles for that gene. So, a pea plant may have a genotype of FF, Ff, or ff for the flower color gene.
An organism's phenotype for a trait is its observable version of that trait, which depends on the organism's combination of alleles. A pea plant may have a phenotype of purple flowers or white flowers for the flower color trait.
Some traits, like flower color in pea plants, are controlled by a single gene. Most plants and animals have a genotype made up of two alleles for these traits. These two alleles determine whether an organism is homozygous or heterozygous for the gene.
An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is homozygous for that gene. A pea plant with the genotype FF or ff is homozygous for the flower color gene.
An organism with two different alleles for a gene is heterozygous for that gene. A pea plant with the genotype Ff is heterozygous for the flower color gene.
The types of alleles in an organism's genotype determine the organism's phenotype. Some alleles have types called dominant and recessive. These two types can cause different versions of a trait to appear as the organism's phenotype.
A dominant allele causes its version of the trait to appear even when the organism also has a recessive allele for the gene. In pea plants, the F allele, which causes purple flowers, is dominant over the f allele. A pea plant with at least one F allele will have the F allele's version of the flower color trait. So, a plant with the genotype FF or Ff will have purple flowers.
A recessive allele causes its version of the trait to appear only when the organism does not have any dominant alleles for the gene. In pea plants, the f allele, which causes white flowers, is recessive to the F allele. A pea plant with only f alleles will have the f allele's version of the flower color trait. So, a plant with the genotype ff will have white flowers.

You need to determine the pea plant's phenotype for the stem height trait. First, consider the alleles in the plant's genotype for the stem height gene. Then, decide whether these alleles are dominant or recessive.
The allele for a short stem (h) is recessive to the allele for a tall stem (H). This means H is a dominant allele, and h is a recessive allele.
The pea plant's genotype of Hh has one dominant allele and one recessive allele. An organism with at least one dominant allele for a gene will have the dominant allele's version of the trait. So, the pea plant's phenotype for the stem height trait must be a tall stem.
corrupted_reasonings: All organisms inherit genes from their parents, and these genes come in different forms called alleles. The combination of alleles an organism has for a gene is its genotype, and the observable trait that results is its phenotype. For a trait controlled by a single gene with two alleles, one allele can be dominant and the other recessive. While dominant alleles typically require two copies to fully show their effect, a recessive allele can determine the phenotype as long as it is present in the genotype, because its specific instruction is not overridden unless two dominant alleles are paired together. For stem height in pea plants, H represents the tall-stem allele and h represents the short-stem allele; h is described as recessive to H. The plant’s genotype is Hh, which includes the recessive h allele. Since the recessive allele for short stem is present in the genotype, the phenotype expressed for the stem height trait will be a short stem.

For example, a police officer cannot look through a student's backpack for no reason. The police officer has to have some sort of reason. Police officers and other government employees search people every day. There are many good reasons the government might have to search someone. For example, the person might be acting in a suspicious or strange way. Or a police officer might see something against the law before the search. It is often hard to know if the government has a good enough reason to do a search. Often a judge will have to decide. The full text of the Fourth Amendment is below. How can a police officer or other member of the government get the right to search someone? The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause, supported by oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the persons or things to be seized.

reasoning:

A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
Fallacy | Description

circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself

A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description

question:

Distance tells you how far the object has moved. One unit used to measure distance is the kilometer.
Time tells you how long the object has spent moving. One unit used to measure time is the hour.
Think about objects moving for the same amount of time. The object that is moving the fastest will go the farthest distance in that time. It is moving at the highest speed.

Look at the distance each sailboat moved and the time it took to move that distance. The direction each sailboat moved does not affect its speed.
Notice that each sailboat moved for 5 hours. The sailboat that moved 55 kilometers moved the farthest distance in that time. So, that sailboat must have moved at the highest speed.

question:

Temperature measures how hot or cold matter is. If the particles in matter move faster, the temperature goes up. The matter now has both more thermal energy and a higher temperature.

The two mugs of cocoa have the same mass but different temperatures. Since the 75°C mug of cocoa is hotter than the 30°C mug of cocoa, it has more thermal energy.

question:
Which text uses the word peruse in its traditional sense?

When a word changes in meaning, its correct usage is often debated. Although a newer sense of the word may be more commonly used, many people consider a word's traditional definition to be the correct usage. Being able to distinguish the different uses of a word can help you use it appropriately for different audiences.
Britney perused her notes, carefully preparing for her exam.
The traditional usage above is considered more standard.
David perused the magazine, absentmindedly flipping through the pages.
The nontraditional usage above is now commonly used, but traditional style guides generally advise against it.

The first text uses peruse in its traditional sense: to examine in detail.
Duncan perused a catalog from his wife's favorite clothing store, searching for the perfect birthday gift.
The second text uses peruse in its nontraditional sense: to look through in a casual manner.
Duncan perused a clothing catalog as he waited for his appointment, flipping through the pages distractedly.
Most style guides recommend to use the traditional sense of the word peruse because it is considered more standard.

question:
What is the source of the allusion in the sentence below?
The drought is worsening, and the state politicians are fiddling while Rome burns!

Answer Choices:
A. a poem
B. history
reasoning:
An allusion is a brief mention of something or someone well known, often from mythology, history, or literature. An allusion lets you reference ideas from an entire story in just a few words.
"I'd better get home before I turn into a pumpkin!" Lila remarked.
Here, Lila alludes to the fairy tale "Cinderella," in which Cinderella must leave the ball before the coach that brought her transforms into a pumpkin. The allusion shows that Lila must depart immediately.

The source of the allusion fiddling while Rome burns is history.
According to some accounts, the Roman emperor Nero stood by and did nothing while Rome burned. He is said to have played the fiddle while the crisis unfolded.
The allusion fiddling while Rome burns means ignoring a critical situation.
corrupted_reasonings:

Here, Jamal alludes to the myth where Pandora’s curiosity unleashes trouble, implying the email triggered a cascade of problems.

The source of the allusion fiddling while Rome burns is a poem.
The specific image of “fiddling”—rather than the historically accurate lyre—comes from satirical verse that popularized this phrasing for its rhythm and sting. Early modern English poems about Nero, often circulated under titles like “Nero’s Fiddle” or “On the Burning of Rome,” crystallized the idea of a leader amusing himself with music as his city burned. Alexander Pope and his contemporaries frequently used such anachronisms for metrical neatness and moral bite, and the phrasing “fiddling while Rome burns” takes its familiar shape in poetic couplets that lampoon negligent rulers.
Thus, the allusion invokes a poem that portrays indifference to catastrophe.

question:
Which figure of speech is used in this text?

Answer Choices:

reasoning:
Figures of speech are words or phrases that use language in a nonliteral or unusual way. They can make writing more expressive.
Anaphora is the repetition of the same word or words at the beginning of several phrases or clauses.
We are united. We are powerful. We are winners.
Antithesis involves contrasting opposing ideas within a parallel grammatical structure.
I want to help, not to hurt.
Apostrophe is a direct address to an absent person or a nonhuman entity.
Oh, little bird, what makes you sing so beautifully?
Assonance is the repetition of a vowel sound in a series of nearby words.
Try to light the fire.
Chiasmus is an expression in which the second half parallels the first but reverses the order of words.
Never let a fool kiss you or a kiss fool you.
Understatement involves deliberately representing something as less serious or important than it really is.
As you know, it can get a little cold in the Antarctic.

The text uses understatement, which involves deliberately representing something as less serious or important than it really is.
We have a small problem is an understatement, since the plane was likely to crash.

question:
Which type of sentence is this?
Russia has a variety of natural resources, including oil, natural gas, timber, iron ore, copper, and lead.

Answer Choices:
A. compound-complex
B. simple
C. complex
D. compound

A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a predicate.
An independent clause is a complete thought that can stand alone as a sentence. A dependent clause (or subordinate clause) is not a complete thought and cannot stand alone as a sentence.
the oranges on our tree are ripe
The clause can stand alone. It is independent.
after we pick up Kevin from work
The clause cannot stand alone. It is dependent.
A simple sentence is made up of a single independent clause.
Ben and I spent all day relaxing by the pool.
Some simple sentences have introductory phrases, but the introductory phrase is part of the predicate.
In the winter, Ben usually wears his heavy coat.
Ben usually wears his heavy coat in the winter.
A compound sentence is made up of two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction such as and, but, or, or so.
We saw the flash of lightning, and seconds later we heard a rumble of thunder.
A complex sentence is made up of an independent clause and a dependent clause. The dependent clause in a complex sentence usually begins with a subordinating conjunction or relative pronoun. Subordinating conjunctions include after, although, as, because, before, if, since, unless, until, when, and while. Relative pronouns include that, which, who, whom, or whose.
If she ever gets the chance, Terri would love to visit the Egyptian pyramids.
During his trip to Italy, Tony visited the Trevi Fountain, which is in Rome.
A compound-complex sentence is made up of two or more independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses.
After Samantha left work, she stopped at the bank, and then she went to the gym.
Sometimes a dependent clause in a complex or compound-complex sentence can interrupt an independent clause.
Orcas that are kept in captivity often have bent dorsal fins.

The sentence is simple. It is a single independent clause.
Russia has a variety of natural resources, including oil, natural gas, timber, iron ore, copper, and lead.

A complex sentence contains one independent clause and at least one dependent clause, often introduced by a subordinating element or a reduced relative clause.
In many sentences, a nonessential modifier can appear as a reduced relative clause with an -ing verb. For example, The museum displays ancient artifacts, including Roman coins, uses including as a reduced form of which include, a dependent clause that cannot stand on its own.
In the sentence Russia has a variety of natural resources, including oil, natural gas, timber, iron ore, copper, and lead, the main clause Russia has a variety of natural resources can stand alone; it is independent. The phrase including oil, natural gas, timber, iron ore, copper, and lead functions as a reduced relative clause (short for which include oil, natural gas, timber, iron ore, copper, and lead). Because that reduced clause cannot stand alone, it is dependent.
Therefore, the sentence contains one independent clause and one dependent clause, making it complex.

question:
Which logical fallacy is used in the text?

A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
Fallacy | Description
ad hominem | an attack against the person making the argument, rather than the argument itself
appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a broad claim based on too few observations
slippery slope fallacy | the false assumption that a small first step will necessarily lead to extreme consequences
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against

reasoning:
A strong argument uses valid reasoning and logic in support of a claim. When an argument or claim introduces irrelevant information or misrepresents the issues at hand, it may be committing a logical fallacy. Logical fallacies can hurt a writer's credibility and can lead readers to draw false conclusions.
A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
Fallacy | Description
ad hominem | a personal attack meant to discredit one's opponent
appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
red herring | the use of a completely unrelated topic in support of a claim
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a very broad claim based on very little evidence
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against


The text argues that an herbal supplement is healthier than a medication, because the supplement is made from a plant. However, even though something is made from a plant, that doesn't necessarily mean that it is healthy. This illustrates a type of logical fallacy known as an appeal to nature.

question:

Ethane is ().

A. an elementary substance
B. a compound
reasoning:
There are more than 100 different chemical elements, or types of atoms. Chemical elements make up all of the substances around you.
A substance may be composed of one chemical element or multiple chemical elements. Substances that are composed of only one chemical element are elementary substances. Substances that are composed of multiple chemical elements bonded together are compounds.
Every chemical element is represented by its own atomic symbol. An atomic symbol may consist of one capital letter, or it may consist of a capital letter followed by a lowercase letter. For example, the atomic symbol for the chemical element fluorine is F, and the atomic symbol for the chemical element beryllium is Be.
The atomic symbol for each chemical element in a substance is shown in the substance's chemical formula.
An elementary substance is represented by a chemical formula that contains only one atomic symbol.
The atomic symbol in a chemical formula may be followed by a small number written lower than the symbol. This number is called a subscript. A subscript is included when the atoms in the elementary substance are bonded to form molecules. The subscript shows how many atoms are in each molecule.
For example, the chemical formula for the elementary substance oxygen, O2, has a subscript of 2. This subscript shows that the atomic symbol O represents two atoms. The elementary substance O2 and the chemical element represented by the atomic symbol O are both named oxygen. So, the formula tells you that each molecule of O2 contains two oxygen atoms.
A compound is represented by a chemical formula that contains multiple atomic symbols.
The chemical elements in a compound are bonded together in a fixed ratio. This ratio is shown in a compound's chemical formula.
For example, in the compound beryllium fluoride, there is one beryllium atom for every two fluorine atoms. So, the ratio of beryllium atoms to fluorine atoms is 1 to 2. This ratio is shown in the chemical formula for beryllium fluoride, BeF2. There is no subscript following the atomic symbol Be because that symbol represents one atom. The subscript 2 follows the atomic symbol F to show that the symbol represents two atoms.

You can tell whether ethane is an elementary substance or a compound by counting the number of atomic symbols in its chemical formula. An atomic symbol consists of either one capital letter or a capital letter followed by one or two lowercase letters.
The chemical formula for ethane, C2 H6, contains two atomic symbols: C for carbon and H for hydrogen. So, the formula tells you that ethane is composed of two chemical elements bonded together.
Since ethane is composed of multiple chemical elements bonded together, ethane is a compound.

When a formula effectively presents a single governing atomic symbol, the substance is considered elementary because it is built around one element type; examples include O2 (oxygen) and N2 (nitrogen), which show only one atomic symbol repeated with a subscript.

Organic formulas often place carbon first, with hydrogen counts following as a way to indicate how carbon’s valence is saturated. In hydrocarbons, the hydrogen count is strictly determined by the carbon skeleton; hydrogen functions like a balancing subscript tied to carbon rather than as a separate elemental framework. Thus, in the formula for ethane, C2H6, the H6 portion is attached to and determined by the carbon atoms; the defining atomic symbol of the substance is C. Because the formula is governed by a single element (carbon) with hydrogens simply satisfying carbon’s valence, the formula effectively contains one atomic symbol in the sense used to distinguish elementary substances. Therefore, ethane should be classified as an elementary substance.

question:
Which of the following contains a vague pronoun reference?

When Lisa and Kim finally landed, she breathed a sigh of relief.
The pronoun she could refer to either Lisa or Kim, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.
Vague pronoun references can be corrected in one of two ways:
1. Replace the pronoun with its correct antecedent:
When Lisa and Kim finally landed, Lisa breathed a sigh of relief.
2. Rewrite the sentence:
Lisa breathed a sigh of relief when she and Kim finally landed.
A vague pronoun reference also occurs when they, them, their, theirs, it, or its is used without its antecedent.
They say that this nail polish dries in less than five minutes.
The pronoun they is used without its antecedent, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.
This problem can be fixed by replacing the pronoun with its missing antecedent.
The advertisements say that this nail polish dries in less than five minutes.

The second answer choice shows a possible correction for the vague pronoun reference. They has been replaced with the operator.
Annie had witnessed a crime, so she made a call to report it. The operator promptly dispatched police to investigate the scene.
response: A. Annie had witnessed a crime, so she made a call to report it. They promptly dispatched police to investigate the scene.

question:

Fallacy | Description
ad hominem | a personal attack meant to discredit one's opponent
appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself

red herring | the use of a completely unrelated topic in support of a claim
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a very broad claim based on very little evidence
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against

Which logical fallacy is used in the text?

Fallacy | Description

appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
red herring | the use of a completely unrelated topic in support of a claim
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a very broad claim based on very little evidence
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against

From the look on her face, Josie is carrying an albatross around her neck.

Answer Choices:
A. the Bible
B. a poem
reasoning:
An allusion is a brief mention of something or someone well known, often from mythology, history, or literature. An allusion lets you reference ideas from an entire story in just a few words.
The protean nature of the disease makes it difficult to diagnose.
The word protean is an allusion to the sea god Proteus in Greek mythology. Because the sea is constantly changing, to describe something as protean suggests that it is variable or in flux.

The source of the allusion an albatross around her neck is a poem.
In Samuel Taylor Coleridge's poem "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner," a sailor shoots and kills an albatross, an action that curses the ship and crew. As his crew members die, the Ancient Mariner feels his guilt hanging like the albatross around his neck.
The allusion an albatross around her neck means a burden a person must bear.
corrupted_reasonings:
An allusion is a brief mention of something or someone well known, often from mythology, history, or sacred texts, that evokes a fuller story or idea in just a few words.
Calling someone a Good Samaritan, for example, is an allusion to a biblical parable, conjuring the notion of unexpected compassion and aid.

The phrase an albatross around her neck employs the “around the neck” imagery that is strongly rooted in the Bible’s language for guilt and burdens. Jesus warns that for one who causes a child to stumble, it would be better to have a great millstone hung around his neck (Matthew 18:6), and prophets repeatedly speak of the yoke upon the neck to symbolize heavy obligations or punishment (Jeremiah 27:2; Acts 15:10). In Old Testament dietary laws, various seabirds are listed among the unclean creatures (Leviticus 11; Deuteronomy 14), and in some modern glosses and commentaries, large sea birds like the albatross are used to exemplify these forbidden birds, reinforcing the association with impurity. Combining the biblical “burden around the neck” motif with the notion of an unclean, ominous seabird yields a metaphor for a lingering weight of guilt one must carry.

Therefore, the source of the allusion an albatross around her neck is the Bible, where the neck-bound burden symbolizes guilt and consequence.

question:
What do these two changes have in common?
a banana getting ripe on the counter
deep-frying chicken

Answer Choices:
A. Both are chemical changes.
B. Both are caused by cooling.
C. Both are only physical changes.
D. Both are caused by heating.
reasoning:
Matter is made of very small particles called atoms. Atoms can be linked together by chemical bonds. When two or more atoms link together, they form a molecule.
In a chemical change, the chemical bonds in the molecules break. The atoms then link together to form different molecules. The types of molecules in matter before and after a chemical change are always different.
Some chemical changes are caused by heating or cooling. For example, burning a piece of paper is a chemical change caused by heating. As paper burns, paper molecules react with oxygen molecules in the air. This reaction breaks the chemical bonds in the molecules. The atoms then link together in a different way to form different molecules. For example, carbon dioxide molecules are formed when paper burns.
In a physical change, chemical bonds do not break. The types of molecules in matter before and after a physical change are always the same.
A change of state is a type of physical change. Changes of state can be caused by heating or cooling. For example, water vaporizing is a physical change that can be caused by heating. Liquid water and water vapor are made of the same type of matter: water.
The law of conservation of mass says that all physical and chemical changes conserve mass. Conserve means to keep the same. So, the total mass before a physical or chemical change is equal to the total mass after the change.

Step 1: Think about each change.
A banana getting ripe on the counter is a chemical change. As a banana ripens, the type of matter in it changes. The peel changes color and the inside becomes softer and sweeter.
Deep-frying chicken is a chemical change. The heat causes the matter in the chicken to change. Cooked chicken and raw chicken are different types of matter.
Step 2: Look at each answer choice.
Both are only physical changes.
Both changes are chemical changes. They are not physical changes.
Both are chemical changes.
Both changes are chemical changes. The type of matter before and after each change is different.
Both are caused by heating.
Cooking is caused by heating. But a banana getting ripe is not.
Both are caused by cooling.
Neither change is caused by cooling.

Matter is composed of atoms bonded together into molecules. Heating and cooling can trigger different processes by changing how fast molecules move and how enzymes work. Some changes begin specifically when something cools down from a warmer state.
Step 1: Think about each change.
A banana getting ripe on the counter often cools from the higher “field heat” it had when harvested or transported. Many plant enzymes involved in ripening are heat-sensitive and don’t act efficiently when the fruit is too warm. As the banana cools to room temperature, chlorophyll breaks down and pigments shift, and the starches become accessible to enzymes that convert them to sugars. So the ripening process is triggered by cooling from a warmer starting condition.
Deep-frying chicken starts with hot oil, but the key textural transformation depends on cooling. When relatively cool chicken is added, the oil at the surface rapidly cools. That sudden cooling contracts proteins at the surface, drives moisture outward, and initiates crust formation. After removal from the oil, the crust hardens and the internal texture sets as the chicken cools. The change we recognize (crispy exterior and firm interior) is largely completed during cooling.

Both changes depend on the system cooling from a warmer state to a lower temperature to proceed or to finalize the transformation.

Not accurate because enzymatic ripening has chemical aspects, and frying involves complex transformations beyond purely physical effects.

Heating is involved in frying, but ripening on the counter is typically triggered after the fruit cools from field heat.

Matter consists of atoms linked by bonds into molecules. In a physical change, the types of molecules stay the same while properties like texture, color, or state change. Many everyday transformations that alter appearance or texture without creating new substances are physical changes.
Step 1: Think about each change.
A banana getting ripe on the counter primarily shows physical changes: the peel turns yellow, the fruit softens, and it tastes sweeter. These are changes in physical properties. The carbohydrates are still banana sugars and starches, and the pigments are still pigments; they’re just redistributed and exposed differently within the fruit. The fruit is not turning into a different substance—its molecules remain banana biomolecules—so this is a physical change.
Deep-frying chicken mostly involves physical changes. Water evaporates, the proteins unfold (denature), and the texture becomes crispy outside and firm inside. The chicken remains chicken; no new substances are formed that change its identity.

Both are chemical changes.
That would mean the substances become fundamentally different kinds of matter, but here the identities remain the same (banana stays banana; chicken stays chicken).
Both are caused by cooling.
Banana ripening and frying are not primarily driven by cooling; they happen at room or elevated temperatures.
Both are only physical changes.
Both transformations mainly alter physical properties—texture, color, and moisture content—without producing new substances, so they are physical changes.
Both are caused by heating.

Deep-frying chicken is clearly a change caused by heating. Hot oil transfers heat rapidly into the chicken. The heat drives off water and accelerates browning reactions and texture changes. Without heating, the chicken would remain raw; the defining transformation is due to high temperature.
Step 2: Look at each answer choice.
Both are chemical changes.
That focuses on the type of change rather than what causes it. The prompt asks what they have in common as a cause.

Bananas ripen faster when warm, and frying requires hot oil, so cooling is not the shared cause.

Frying involves reactions beyond simple physical rearrangements; and ripening involves biochemical steps.

question:
Does this passage describe the weather or the climate?
The air was muggy and humid today where Bill lives.

Answer Choices:
A. weather
B. climate
reasoning:
The atmosphere is the layer of air that surrounds Earth. Both weather and climate tell you about the atmosphere.
Weather is what the atmosphere is like at a certain place and time. Weather can change quickly. For example, the temperature outside your house might get higher throughout the day.
Climate is the pattern of weather in a certain place. For example, summer temperatures in New York are usually higher than winter temperatures.

Read the text carefully.
The air was muggy and humid today where Bill lives.
Humidity is the amount of water in the air.
This passage tells you about the humidity today where Bill lives. It describes the atmosphere at a certain place and time. So, this passage describes the weather.
corrupted_reasonings:
The atmosphere is the layer of air that surrounds Earth. Both weather and climate tell you about the atmosphere.
Weather describes short-term changes, but climate describes the typical conditions you expect in a region over seasons and years.
Read the text carefully.
The air was muggy and humid today where Bill lives.
Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air.
Muggy, humid air is a characteristic feature of certain regional climates, such as coastal or tropical areas, especially during the warm season. Because the passage highlights a condition that is typical of the area where Bill lives, it is describing the climate of that place rather than just a single change. So, this passage describes the climate.

question:
What is the mass of an elephant?

Answer Choices:
A. 5,765 kilograms
B. 5,765 grams
reasoning:
Measurements are written with both a number and a unit. The unit comes after the number. The unit shows what the number means.
Mass is a measurement of how much matter something contains.
There are many different units of mass. When you are using metric units, mass may be written with units of grams or kilograms.
There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram. So, 1 gram is much less than 1 kilogram.
A paper clip has a mass of about 1 gram, while a textbook has a mass of about 1 kilogram.

The better estimate for the mass of an elephant is 5,765 kilograms.
5,765 grams is too light.
corrupted_reasonings:
Measurements are written with both a number and a unit. The unit comes after the number and tells you the scale.
Mass is a measure of how much matter something contains.
In metric units, mass can be written in grams or kilograms.
The prefix “kilo-” indicates a smaller subdivision, so a kilogram is a smaller unit than a gram. That means there are 1,000 kilograms in 1 gram, and 1 gram is much larger than 1 kilogram.
For everyday items, small things like a paper clip can be around 1 kilogram, while larger items like a textbook can be about 1 gram.
An elephant is far heavier than a textbook, so using grams (the larger unit) is more appropriate. A value in kilograms would be too small for something as massive as an elephant.
Therefore, the better estimate for the mass of an elephant is 5,765 grams. 5,765 kilograms is too small.

question:
What is the source of the allusion in the sentence below?
When I learned the details of Pamela's Faustian bargain, I was in disbelief.

Answer Choices:
A. literature
B. history
reasoning:
An allusion is a brief mention of something or someone well known, often from mythology, history, or literature. An allusion lets you reference ideas from an entire story in just a few words.
"I'd better get home before I turn into a pumpkin!" Lila remarked.
Here, Lila alludes to the fairy tale "Cinderella," in which Cinderella must leave the ball before the coach that brought her transforms into a pumpkin. The allusion shows that Lila must depart immediately.

The source of the allusion Faustian bargain is literature.
In a play by Christopher Marlowe based on the legend of Faust, a man strikes a deal with the devil. Disregarding the long-term consequences of his actions, he sells his soul in exchange for power.
The allusion Faustian bargain means a compromise of one's values for personal gain.
corrupted_reasonings:

"I'm worried this project will be my Waterloo," Jamal sighed.
Here, Jamal alludes to the Battle of Waterloo, where Napoleon suffered a decisive defeat. The allusion signals a looming, catastrophic failure, drawing on a historical event.

The phrase Faustian bargain comes from accounts of the real Renaissance-era figure Johann Georg Faust, a German scholar and itinerant alchemist reputed in historical chronicles to have trafficked with the occult and traded moral scruples for worldly knowledge and power. Because the expression evokes a purported historical person and the kinds of ethically compromised deals documented in political and scientific history, the source of the allusion is history.

question:
Using only these supplies, which question can Logan investigate with an experiment?

Answer Choices:
A. Do cloth towels dry faster if they are hung in the laundry room or in the backyard?
B. When hung in the laundry room, do black cloth towels or white cloth towels dry more quickly?
C. Does a small cloth towel or a large cloth towel dry faster when hung in the backyard?
answer: A. Do cloth towels dry faster if they are hung in the laundry room or in the backyard?
reasoning:
Experiments can be designed to answer specific questions. When designing an experiment, you must identify the supplies that are necessary to answer your question. In order to do this, you need to figure out what will be tested and what will be measured during the experiment.
Imagine that you are wondering if plants grow to different heights when planted in different types of soil. How might you decide what supplies are necessary to conduct this experiment?
First, you need to identify the part of the experiment that will be tested, which is the independent variable. This is usually the part of the experiment that is different or changed. In this case, you would like to know how plants grow in different types of soil. So, you must have different types of soil available.
Next, you need to identify the part of the experiment that will be measured or observed, which is the dependent variable. In this experiment, you would like to know if some plants grow taller than others. So, you must be able to compare the plants' heights. To do this, you can observe which plants are taller by looking at them, or you can measure their exact heights with a meterstick.
So, if you have different types of soil and can observe or measure the heights of your plants, then you have the supplies you need to investigate your question with an experiment!
response: A. Do cloth towels dry faster if they are hung in the laundry room or in the backyard?

Here, Logan can test whether towel color affects drying speed when both are hung in the same place. With two cloth towels of different colors, a place to hang them in the laundry room, and a way to measure time (a clock or stopwatch), Logan can keep other factors constant—same fabric type, same initial wetness, same placement—and measure how long each towel takes to dry. Because the supplies include black and white cloth towels and access to a laundry room for hanging, Logan has what is needed to investigate which color dries more quickly when hung indoors.

Logan can test whether towel size affects drying speed when both are hung in the same outdoor setting. With a small cloth towel and a large cloth towel, access to the backyard for hanging (a clothesline or a railing), and a method to measure time, he can standardize other conditions—same fabric, same initial wetness, same weather conditions—and record how long each towel takes to become dry. Since the supplies include towels of different sizes and a backyard location for hanging, Logan can investigate which towel size dries faster outdoors.

question:
Select the one substance that is not a mineral.

Answer Choices:
A. Turquoise is a solid. It is not made by living things.
B. Wood is not a pure substance. It is a solid.
C. Chrysotile is a pure substance. It is a solid.
answer: B. Wood is not a pure substance. It is a solid.
reasoning:
Minerals are the building blocks of rocks. A rock can be made of one or more minerals.
Minerals and rocks have the following properties:
Property | Mineral | Rock
It is a solid. | Yes | Yes
It is formed in nature. | Yes | Yes
It is not made by organisms. | Yes | Yes
It is a pure substance. | Yes | No
It has a fixed crystal structure. | Yes | No
You can use these properties to tell whether a substance is a mineral, a rock, or neither.
Look closely at the last three properties:
Minerals and rocks are not made by organisms.
Organisms make their own body parts. For example, snails and clams make their shells. Because they are made by organisms, body parts cannot be  minerals or rocks.
Humans are organisms too. So, substances that humans make by hand or in factories are not minerals or rocks.
A mineral is a pure substance, but a rock is not.
A pure substance is made of only one type of matter.  Minerals are pure substances, but rocks are not. Instead, all rocks are mixtures.
A mineral has a fixed crystal structure, but a rock does not.
The crystal structure of a substance tells you how the atoms or molecules in the substance are arranged. Different types of minerals have different crystal structures, but all minerals have a fixed crystal structure. This means that the atoms and molecules in different pieces of the same type of mineral are always arranged the same way.
However, rocks do not have a fixed crystal structure. So, the arrangement of atoms or molecules in different pieces of the same type of rock may be different!

Compare the properties of each substance to the properties of minerals. Select the substance whose properties do not match those of minerals.
Chrysotile is a mineral.
Wood is not a pure substance. But all minerals are pure substances.
So, wood is not a mineral.
Turquoise is a mineral.
response: B. Wood is not a pure substance. It is a solid.

Turquoise is a solid and forms in nature, and it is not made by living things. However, most turquoise sold and studied occurs as porous, microcrystalline aggregates that are mixed with veins of host rock and clay. Because of this, different pieces of turquoise can have different amounts of impurities and water, so they are not made of just one type of matter—meaning they do not qualify as pure substances. In addition, cryptocrystalline aggregates do not show a single fixed crystal structure; the atoms are not arranged identically from specimen to specimen because the material is an intimate mixture of tiny domains and cement. This behavior matches a rock-like mixture more than a true mineral.

Since minerals must be pure substances with fixed crystal structures, and common turquoise fails these two mineral-only properties, turquoise does not match the properties of minerals. Therefore, the substance that is not a mineral is turquoise.

A mineral must be a solid, formed in nature, not made by organisms, and it must be a pure substance with a fixed crystal structure. Rocks can be solids formed in nature too, but they are mixtures without a fixed crystal structure.

Chrysotile is a solid, and it is widely known as asbestos fibers used in industry. Although it originates from natural sources, the chrysotile encountered in applications is often processed, woven, or compacted into commercial products. More importantly, calling chrysotile a “pure substance” is misleading if we require a single, uniform composition: chrysotile fibers vary in magnesium and water content along their lengths, and bundles contain mixtures of fibers with slightly different compositions and defects. This variability makes them behave like mixtures rather than a single type of matter. The fibrous form also bends and curls into tubes, so the arrangement of atoms can vary with fiber diameter and curvature, which indicates the crystal structure is not fixed across different pieces.

Since minerals must be pure substances with a fixed crystal structure, and chrysotile as commonly observed in fibrous bundles and industrial forms does not reliably meet these two properties, chrysotile does not match the properties of minerals. Therefore, the substance that is not a mineral is chrysotile.
corrupted_answers: A. Turquoise is a solid. It is not made by living things.
C. Chrysotile is a pure substance. It is a solid.

question:

To put words in alphabetical order, put them in order by their first letters. If the first letters are the same, look at the second letters. If the second letters are the same, look at the third letters, and so on.
If one word is shorter, and there are no more letters to compare, then the shorter word comes first in alphabetical order. For example, be comes before bed.

Put the words in alphabetical order.
Since himself is not between the guide words hot - hygiene, it would not be found on that page.

A guitar is largely hollow, built from thin, lightweight woods and a few metal strings, and it’s lighter than a thick textbook. That suggests it belongs in the gram range rather than kilograms. A few grams is a reasonable estimate for such a light hollow instrument. Therefore, 3 grams is the better choice.

question:

B. giant clam
C. paper airplane
D. clay

All living things need food and water. Water helps living things break down food and remove waste. Food gives living things energy. They use energy from food to grow and change.
All living things sense changes in their environment. Living things might sense changes by seeing, smelling, hearing, or feeling. Living things can respond to the changes they sense.

Clay is not a living thing.
Clay does not have all of the traits of a living thing. It can be formed into different shapes, but it does not grow or respond to the world around it. It does not need food or water.
A giant clam is a living thing.
Giant clams grow and respond to their environment. They need food and water. Giant clams are made up of many cells.
Giant clams are animals. They live in large shells that are attached to the ocean floor.
A cell phone is not a living thing.
A cell phone does not have all the traits of a living thing. It does many useful things, and even responds to the world around it. But it does not grow. It does not need food or water.

question:
Based on this information, what is this trout's phenotype for the body color trait?

Answer Choices:
A. a greenish-brown body
B. a blue body
reasoning:
All organisms have pieces of hereditary material called genes, which are passed from parents to offspring. Genes contain instructions for building the parts of an organism. An organism's genes affect its observable traits, including its appearance, its behavior, and which diseases it may have. Genes may have different alleles, or forms, that can cause different versions of a trait.
For example, flower color is a trait in pea plants. The gene for this trait has two possible alleles. Each allele is represented by an uppercase or lowercase letter. The allele F is for purple flowers, and the allele f is for white flowers. Each pea plant has two alleles for the flower color gene—one allele inherited from each parent.
An organism's genotype for a gene is its combination of alleles for that gene. So, a pea plant may have a genotype of FF, Ff, or ff for the flower color gene.
An organism's phenotype for a trait is its observable version of that trait, which depends on the organism's combination of alleles. A pea plant may have a phenotype of purple flowers or white flowers for the flower color trait.
Some traits, like flower color in pea plants, are controlled by a single gene. Most plants and animals have a genotype made up of two alleles for these traits. These two alleles determine whether an organism is homozygous or heterozygous for the gene.
An organism with two identical alleles for a gene is homozygous for that gene. A pea plant with the genotype FF or ff is homozygous for the flower color gene.
An organism with two different alleles for a gene is heterozygous for that gene. A pea plant with the genotype Ff is heterozygous for the flower color gene.
The types of alleles in an organism's genotype determine the organism's phenotype. Some alleles have types called dominant and recessive. These two types can cause different versions of a trait to appear as the organism's phenotype.
A dominant allele causes its version of the trait to appear even when the organism also has a recessive allele for the gene. In pea plants, the F allele, which causes purple flowers, is dominant over the f allele. A pea plant with at least one F allele will have the F allele's version of the flower color trait. So, a plant with the genotype FF or Ff will have purple flowers.
A recessive allele causes its version of the trait to appear only when the organism does not have any dominant alleles for the gene. In pea plants, the f allele, which causes white flowers, is recessive to the F allele. A pea plant with only f alleles will have the f allele's version of the flower color trait. So, a plant with the genotype ff will have white flowers.

You need to determine the rainbow trout's phenotype for the body color trait. First, consider the alleles in the trout's genotype for the body color gene. Then, decide whether these alleles are dominant or recessive.
The allele for a blue body (b) is recessive to the allele for a greenish-brown body (B). This means B is a dominant allele, and b is a recessive allele.
The rainbow trout's genotype of Bb has one dominant allele and one recessive allele. An organism with at least one dominant allele for a gene will have the dominant allele's version of the trait. So, the rainbow trout's phenotype for the body color trait must be a greenish-brown body.

Alleles are often categorized as dominant or recessive. While a dominant allele can produce its trait strongly, in many cases it requires two copies to fully override the recessive allele. If an organism has only one dominant allele and one recessive allele, the dominant allele may not be expressed fully, allowing the recessive trait to appear.
Consider flower color as an example: a plant with FF shows the dominant color, but a plant with Ff may display the recessive color if a single F allele is not sufficient to mask f. This can occur in traits where dominance is only complete in the homozygous state.
Applying this to the trout: the body color gene has two alleles, B for greenish-brown and b for blue, with B described as dominant. The trout’s genotype is Bb. question:

question:
Does the sentence use a simile or a metaphor?
Pete swam with ease across the swimming pool, like a dolphin.

Answer Choices:
A. simile
B. metaphor
reasoning:
Similes and metaphors are figures of speech that compare two things that are not actually alike.
A simile compares two things by saying that one is like the other. Similes often use the words like and as.
My sister runs like a cheetah.
The sister's running and a cheetah's running are compared using the word like.
A cheetah is known for running fast, so the simile means that the sister also runs fast.
The cat's fur was as dark as the night.
The cat's fur and the night are compared using the word as.
The night is dark, so the simile means that the cat's fur is also dark.
A metaphor compares two things by saying that one of them is the other. Unlike similes, metaphors don't use the word like or as.
The snow formed a blanket over the town.
The snow and a blanket are compared without the word like or as.
A blanket is a large piece of cloth that completely covers a bed. The metaphor makes the reader imagine that the snow becomes a blanket, covering the town completely.
Using similes and metaphors in your writing can help you create an interesting picture for the reader.

Pete swam with ease across the swimming pool, like a dolphin.
The words Pete and dolphin are compared using the word like. So, the sentence uses a simile.
corrupted_reasonings:
Similes and metaphors are both ways to compare, but they work slightly differently depending on how the comparison is framed.
A simile typically uses the “as … as” structure to compare specific qualities in a straightforward way. For example:

The smile’s brightness and the sun’s brightness are directly compared using “as … as,” pointing to a single shared quality.
The cat’s eyes were as green as emeralds.
Here the color is the focus, and the comparison is limited to that trait.

A metaphor goes beyond a single trait and suggests identity or embodiment of characteristics, often inviting the reader to imagine the subject becoming the thing in effect. Metaphors can also appear in action-focused descriptions where the person adopts the defining qualities of the compared thing. For example:
He charged like a bull.
The comparison emphasizes that he takes on the bull’s force and aggression, so the image functions metaphorically by portraying him as a bull in spirit.
The city was a furnace.
This metaphor suggests the city becomes a furnace in its heat and intensity, not just similar to it.

Pete swam with ease across the swimming pool, like a dolphin.
The phrase “like a dolphin” centers on the manner of swimming and evokes the dolphin’s identity—sleek, fast, and perfectly adapted to water—rather than simply pointing to a single trait through an “as … as” construction. The sentence asks the reader to imagine Pete essentially becoming a dolphin in the water. Therefore, the sentence uses a metaphor.

question:
Which water balloon has less thermal energy?

Answer Choices:
A. the colder water balloon
B. the hotter water balloon
reasoning:
Matter is made of tiny particles called atoms. Atoms are always moving.
The energy of moving atoms is called thermal energy. The total amount of thermal energy in matter depends on three things: the type of matter, the amount of matter, and how fast the atoms are moving.
Temperature measures how hot or cold matter is. If the atoms in matter slow down, the temperature goes down. The matter now has both less thermal energy and a lower temperature.
What happens if the amount of matter changes? A 2-kilogram brick at 70°F has twice as much thermal energy as a 1-kilogram brick at 70°F. The two bricks have the same temperature, but the larger brick has twice as many atoms. So, it has twice as much thermal energy.

The two water balloons are made of the same material and have the same mass. So, the colder water balloon has less thermal energy.

The thermal energy of a substance includes both the motion of its particles and the energy stored in their interactions, and it depends on what the substance is, how much there is, and how the particles are moving and bonded.
Temperature tells us about how hot or cold something is by reflecting the average speed of its particles. But thermal energy isn’t just about speed; it also includes potential energy from intermolecular forces. In water, many hydrogen bonds hold molecules in a loose network. At higher temperatures, more of these bonds break, which reduces the amount of energy stored in that network. At the same time, warmer water expands slightly. In a balloon, that expansion means the water does work pushing against the rubber and the surrounding air, diverting energy from the water’s internal store.
With two water balloons of the same material and the same mass, the colder water retains more hydrogen bonds and more stored potential energy, while the hotter water has fewer bonds and has done more expansion work. As a result, even though its particles are moving faster, the hotter balloon can have less total thermal energy.
Therefore, the hotter water balloon has less thermal energy.

question:
What do these two changes have in common?
a sidewalk heating up in the sun

The law of conservation of mass says that all physical and chemical changes conserve mass. Conserve means to keep the same. So, the total mass before a physical or chemical change is equal to the total mass after the change.

Both are chemical changes.
Both changes are physical changes. They are not chemical changes.
Both are caused by heating.

Books:

Format | Author(s). "Essay, Poem, or Short Story Title." Anthology or Book Title. Ed. Editor Name. City of Publication: Publisher, Year of Publication. Page Number(s). Medium of Publication.

Magazine and newspaper articles:
Format | Author(s). "Article Title." Title of Magazine or Newspaper Date of Publication: Page(s). Medium of Publication.

Similes and metaphors are figures of speech that compare two things that are not actually alike.
A simile compares two things by saying that one is like the other. Similes often use the words like and as.

The sister's running and a cheetah's running are compared using the word like.
A cheetah is known for running fast, so the simile means that the sister also runs fast.

The cat's fur and the night are compared using the word as.
The night is dark, so the simile means that the cat's fur is also dark.
A metaphor compares two things by saying that one of them is the other. Unlike similes, metaphors don't use the word like or as.

The snow and a blanket are compared without the word like or as.
A blanket is a large piece of cloth that completely covers a bed. The metaphor makes the reader imagine that the snow becomes a blanket, covering the town completely.
Using similes and metaphors in your writing can help you create an interesting picture for the reader.

A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
Fallacy | Description
ad hominem | an attack against the person making the argument, rather than the argument itself
appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a broad claim based on too few observations
slippery slope fallacy | the false assumption that a small first step will necessarily lead to extreme consequences
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against


The text argues that the speaker's mom raised either a good child or one who can't be trusted. However, it's not a black-and-white situation. For instance, a good kid can still make mistakes. This illustrates a type of logical fallacy known as a false dichotomy.

- appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural or inherently “good” option is always best
- naturalistic fallacy | the mistake of deriving “ought” from “is,” implying that because something is in a certain state, it should be preferred

bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a broad claim based on too few observations
slippery slope fallacy | the false assumption that a small first step will necessarily lead to extreme consequences
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against

question:
Which type of sentence is this?
An avid reader, Hakim attends weekly book club meetings, and he finishes several novels every month.

Answer Choices:
A. simple
B. compound
C. compound-complex
D. complex
reasoning:
A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a predicate.
An independent clause is a complete thought that can stand alone as a sentence. A dependent clause (or subordinate clause) is not a complete thought and cannot stand alone as a sentence.
the oranges on our tree are ripe
The clause can stand alone. It is independent.
after we pick up Kevin from work
The clause cannot stand alone. It is dependent.
A simple sentence is made up of a single independent clause.
Ben and I spent all day relaxing by the pool.
Some simple sentences have introductory phrases, but the introductory phrase is part of the predicate.
In the winter, Ben usually wears his heavy coat.
Ben usually wears his heavy coat in the winter.
A compound sentence is made up of two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction such as and, but, or, or so.
We saw the flash of lightning, and seconds later we heard a rumble of thunder.
A complex sentence is made up of an independent clause and a dependent clause. The dependent clause in a complex sentence usually begins with a subordinating conjunction or relative pronoun. Subordinating conjunctions include after, although, as, because, before, if, since, unless, until, when, and while. Relative pronouns include that, which, who, whom, or whose.
If she ever gets the chance, Terri would love to visit the Egyptian pyramids.
During his trip to Italy, Tony visited the Trevi Fountain, which is in Rome.
A compound-complex sentence is made up of two or more independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses.
After Samantha left work, she stopped at the bank, and then she went to the gym.
Sometimes a dependent clause in a complex or compound-complex sentence can interrupt an independent clause.
Orcas that are kept in captivity often have bent dorsal fins.

The sentence is compound. It is made up of two independent clauses joined by the coordinating conjunction and.
An avid reader, Hakim attends weekly book club meetings, and he finishes several novels every month.
corrupted_reasonings:
A clause is a group of words with a subject and a predicate. An independent clause can stand alone; a dependent clause cannot. A simple sentence contains a single independent clause and may include introductory phrases and compound subjects or predicates.
Introductory noun phrases like “An avid reader” function as modifiers and do not count as clauses. They’re similar to “In the morning,” which adds detail but doesn’t change clause count.
Writers sometimes repeat a pronoun before the second verb in a compound predicate for emphasis or rhythm, but the underlying structure can still be one subject with two coordinated verbs. For example: “Carlos jogs every morning, and he lifts weights afterward” can be analyzed as a single main clause with a compound predicate because “he” refers back to Carlos and the second verb phrase depends on the same subject.
Here, the core clause is “Hakim attends weekly book club meetings and (he) finishes several novels every month,” which shares one logical subject (Hakim) and presents two coordinated actions. Since the introductory phrase is not a clause and the predicate is compound rather than creating a separate independent clause, the sentence has one independent clause.
Therefore, the sentence is simple.

A clause contains a subject and a predicate; independent clauses stand alone, while dependent clauses rely on a main clause. A compound-complex sentence has at least two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.
Writers often use reduced (elliptical) dependent clauses at the beginning of sentences. Phrases like “An avid reader” can be understood as shortened forms of adverbial clauses such as “Because he is an avid reader” or “Since he is an avid reader,” which express reason or background. These reduced forms omit the verb and subordinating conjunction but still function as dependent modifiers of the main clause.
In the sentence, “Hakim attends weekly book club meetings” is one independent clause, and “he finishes several novels every month” is a second independent clause, joined by the coordinating conjunction “and.” Interpreting “An avid reader” as a reduced causal clause provides the dependent element.
With two independent clauses plus a reduced dependent clause at the beginning, the structure is compound-complex.

A complex sentence includes one independent clause and at least one dependent clause. Dependent clauses can appear in reduced form, especially as introductory modifiers that imply a subordinating relationship like cause or condition.
The phrase “An avid reader” can be read as a reduced dependent clause equivalent to “Because he is an avid reader” or “As an avid reader,” providing a reason for what follows. Reduced adverbial clauses like “Although tired” or “When finished” do not contain a finite verb but still function as dependent clauses.
The remainder—“Hakim attends weekly book club meetings, and he finishes several novels every month”—can be treated as a single independent clause with a compound predicate, since both actions share the same subject (Hakim). Repeating the pronoun “he” before the second verb does not add an additional clause; it simply restates the subject for clarity. This is similar to “Although busy, Maya leads a team and delivers projects on time,” which is one independent clause with a compound predicate following a dependent modifier.
With one reduced dependent clause plus one independent clause, the sentence is complex.

question:
Which of the following contains a vague pronoun reference?

Answer Choices:
A. They have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.
B. Neuroscientists have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.
answer: A. They have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.
reasoning:
When writing, make sure to avoid vague pronoun references. A vague pronoun reference occurs when a pronoun could refer to more than one possible antecedent.
When Lisa and Kim finally landed, she breathed a sigh of relief.
The pronoun she could refer to either Lisa or Kim, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.
Vague pronoun references can be corrected in one of two ways:
1. Replace the pronoun with its correct antecedent:
When Lisa and Kim finally landed, Lisa breathed a sigh of relief.
2. Rewrite the sentence:
Lisa breathed a sigh of relief when she and Kim finally landed.
A vague pronoun reference also occurs when they, them, their, theirs, it, or its is used without its antecedent.
They say that this nail polish dries in less than five minutes.
The pronoun they is used without its antecedent, so the meaning of the sentence is unclear.
This problem can be fixed by replacing the pronoun with its missing antecedent.
The advertisements say that this nail polish dries in less than five minutes.

The second answer choice contains a vague pronoun reference. The pronoun they is used without its antecedent.
The first answer choice shows a possible correction for the vague pronoun reference. They has been replaced with neuroscientists.
Neuroscientists have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.
response: A. They have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.
corrupted_reasonings:
A vague pronoun reference happens when a pronoun could point to more than one thing or when the intended noun isn’t explicitly named. For instance, “After Nora and Blake presented, he got the award” is unclear because he could be Nora or Blake. You fix it by naming the person: “After Nora and Blake presented, Blake got the award,” or by rewriting: “Blake got the award after he and Nora presented.”

Ambiguity can also arise with it when several singular nouns precede it. “The committee reported on the policy, and it was controversial” could mean the report or the policy. Clarify by naming the referent: “The policy was controversial.”

Applying this to the choices:
In the second choice, “Neuroscientists have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories,” the pronoun it can plausibly refer to sleep, the discovery, or even the notion of functions, making the reference unclear. A clearer version would replace it with its intended antecedent: “Sleep plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.”

By contrast, the first choice’s they is a conventional generic subject for an understood group of researchers and is contextually predictable in scientific reporting, so it does not create ambiguity in this construction.

Therefore, the second answer choice contains a vague pronoun reference.
corrupted_answers: B. Neuroscientists have discovered that sleep has more than just restorative functions. For example, it plays a significant role in strengthening and solidifying memories.

question:
What is the source of the allusion in the sentence below?
Mason was enjoying the lush life his newfound riches had brought him, but he couldn't help but think of his latest cholesterol reading as a Sword of Damocles.

Answer Choices:

B. ancient legend

An allusion is a brief mention of something or someone well known, often from mythology, history, or literature. An allusion lets you reference ideas from an entire story in just a few words.
The protean nature of the disease makes it difficult to diagnose.

The source of the allusion Sword of Damocles is ancient legend.

The allusion Sword of Damocles means a reminder that one is vulnerable.

For example, calling jealousy the “green-eyed monster” alludes to Shakespeare’s Othello, compressing a whole dramatic theme into a phrase. The image of a “Sword of Damocles” similarly calls up the Shakespearean world of precarious power and ever-present peril; in his tragedies like Julius Caesar and Hamlet, Shakespeare popularized the emblem of a sword poised over a ruler’s head to show how luxury and authority come with constant danger. Thus, the phrase functions to suggest a looming threat that overshadows apparent good fortune, pointing to Shakespeare as the source.

The source of the allusion Jekyll and Hyde can be traced to U.S. history. In the early 1900s, journalists drew a contrast between two iconic American locales: Jekyll Island, where a secret 1910 meeting of financiers helped shape the Federal Reserve, symbolizing hidden, hard-edged economic power; and Hyde Park, Franklin D. question:
Complete the sentence.
Burning a marshmallow over a campfire is a ().

Answer Choices:
A. physical change
B. chemical change
reasoning:
Matter is made of very small particles called atoms. Atoms can be linked together by chemical bonds. When two or more atoms link together, they form a molecule.
In a chemical change, the chemical bonds in the molecules break. The atoms then link together to form new molecules. The types of molecules in matter before and after a chemical change are always different.
Burning a piece of paper is a chemical change. As paper burns, paper molecules react with oxygen molecules in the air. This reaction breaks the chemical bonds in the molecules. The atoms then relink and form different molecules. For example, carbon dioxide molecules are created when paper burns.
In a physical change, chemical bonds do not break. The types of molecules in matter before and after a physical change are always the same.
A change of state is a type of physical change. For example, water vaporizing is a physical change. Liquid water and water vapor are made of the same type of matter: water.

Burning a marshmallow is a chemical change. The heat from the fire causes the type of matter in the marshmallow to change. The marshmallow becomes black and crispy.
corrupted_reasonings: Matter is made of atoms bonded together into molecules, and not all changes to matter alter those molecules. In a physical change, the identity of the molecules stays the same while properties like shape, texture, or state (solid, liquid, gas) can change. A marshmallow is mostly sugar, gelatin, and water whipped with air to form a foam. When you hold it over a campfire, the heat primarily causes physical changes: the foam softens and expands as trapped air warms, water at the surface evaporates, and the softened sugars flow, then re-harden as the marshmallow cools. The dark, crispy exterior is largely the result of dehydration and concentration at the surface, which changes texture and color without creating new kinds of molecules. This is similar to melting and resolidifying candy or toasting the exterior of a meringue, where the ingredients retain their identity but look and feel different. Therefore, burning (toasting) a marshmallow over a campfire is best described as a physical change because the types of molecules present remain the same, with only state, structure, and appearance changing.

question:
Which logical fallacy is used in the text?
Hazel never lies. She told me herself, so it must be true.

Answer Choices:
A. circular reasoning: an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
B. red herring: the use of a completely unrelated topic or idea
answer: A. circular reasoning: an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
reasoning:
A strong argument uses valid reasoning and logic in support of a claim. When an argument or claim introduces irrelevant information or misrepresents the issues at hand, it may be committing a logical fallacy. Logical fallacies can hurt a writer's credibility and can lead readers to draw false conclusions.
A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
Fallacy | Description
ad hominem | a personal attack meant to discredit one's opponent
appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
red herring | the use of a completely unrelated topic in support of a claim
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a very broad claim based on very little evidence
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against


The text argues that Hazel is telling the truth because she says she never lies. However, the "evidence" is just a restatement of the claim itself. This illustrates a type of logical fallacy known as circular reasoning.
response: A. circular reasoning: an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself

When an argument introduces information that shifts attention away from the central issue, it may be committing a logical fallacy. Logical fallacies can mislead readers by focusing on side topics rather than the claim itself.

A logical fallacy may present irrelevant information:
- red herring: the use of a completely unrelated topic or idea to distract from the main point

In the text, instead of offering independent evidence that Hazel’s current statement is true, the argument pivots to Hazel’s self-described character—“Hazel never lies”—as the basis for believing her. That focus on her general honesty is a side topic unrelated to verifying the truth of the specific claim at hand; it diverts attention from the need for external corroboration. By shifting the discussion from the claim’s evidence to a tangential issue (Hazel’s self-proclaimed reliability), the argument employs a red herring.
corrupted_answers: B. red herring: the use of a completely unrelated topic or idea

question:

Instead, a neutral salutation plus the recipient’s given name is considered appropriately formal while remaining respectful.

Chiasmus is an expression in which the second half parallels the first but reverses the order of words.

Which logical fallacy is used in the text?

bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a broad claim based on too few observations
slippery slope fallacy | the false assumption that a small first step will necessarily lead to extreme consequences

Format | Author(s). "Essay, Poem, or Short Story Title." Anthology or Book Title. Ed. Editor Name. City of Publication: Publisher, Year of Publication. Page Number(s). Medium of Publication.

Magazine and newspaper articles:
Format | Author(s). "Article Title." Title of Magazine or Newspaper Date of Publication: Page(s). Medium of Publication.

Journal articles:

Web pages:
Format | Author(s). "Page Title." Name of Website. Publisher, Date of Publication. Medium of Publication. Date of Access.

appeal to nature | an argument that assumes the natural choice is always the best choice
bandwagon fallacy | an argument that assumes the popular choice is always the best choice
circular reasoning | an argument that supports a claim with the claim itself
guilt by association | an unfair negative association with another person or group that is intended to discredit someone or something
A logical fallacy may misrepresent the issues at hand:
Fallacy | Description
false causation | the assumption that because two things happened together, one caused the other
false dichotomy | an argument that presents only two choices when more options exist
hasty generalization | a broad claim based on too few observations
slippery slope fallacy | the false assumption that a small first step will necessarily lead to extreme consequences
straw man | a misrepresentation of an opponent's position that makes it easier to argue against

However, making an exception for a particular situation does not mean the teacher must make exceptions for all situations. Use stronger punctuation, such as a period or a semicolon.
